title: Banded queue with voluntary degradation for volatile spike handling
creator: Priya Mehta
description:
Problem: During short, high-intensity traffic spikes (e.g., marketing campaigns, model-experiment churn), some tenants consume disproportionate serving capacity, causing noisy neighbor effects and SLO violations for others. Existing admission controllers are binary (accept/reject) or use coarse token-buckets per-tenant which either throttle too aggressively or allow bursty overloads.

Goal: Implement a banded queue + voluntary degradation system that: (1) assigns requests into latency bands based on tenant priority and request characteristics, (2) provides a reclaimable soft-quota per-tenant that prefers graceful degradation (lower-cost model variant, compressed response, or partial output) over hard drop, and (3) wires into circuit breakers and cross-region failover so behavior is consistent during cascading failures. The system should be observable and tunable via Console rollout UI and expose an opt-in per-tenant profile for tradeoffs.

Scope: prototype and Canary for Hosted API + Dedicated; design integration points for Private. This ticket covers design, server-side admission control + queue behavior, and end-to-end test harness. Client SDK changes are scoped separately.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant soft-quota accepts a configurable degradation chain (list of fallback actions) and applies them automatically when soft-quota is exceeded
Requests are placed into at least three latency bands (fast, normal, background) with eviction from lowest band first under pressure
Degradation actions available: model-variant fallback, max-output-tokens truncation, response compression, and non-blocking placeholder response; at least two implemented for Canary
System integrates with existing circuit-breaker: if region-level circuit triggers, banded-queue shifts all affected requests to background band and applies pre-configured degradation profile
Dashboard shows per-tenant soft-quota usage, band occupancy, and degradation events with links to SLO impact graphs
End-to-end load test demonstrates 60% fewer P99 latency SLO violations for high-priority tenants compared to current token-bucket baseline under a synthetic marketing spike
Rollout plan and runbook added to Console runbooks and on-call rotations updated

notes: Design trade-offs considered: maintaining strict fairness vs. preferring graceful degradation for higher overall availability; chose policy that biases toward preserving high-priority tenant SLOs with configurable tenant-level override.
Soft-quota semantics: soft quota consumption accrues per-minute and decays with configurable half-life to allow burst recovery without manual intervention.
Eviction policy: background band uses LRU w/ priority aging; experiments show LRU+aging reduces repeated churn for large streaming clients.
Fallback actions are ordered and rated by cost delta and quality delta; the policy engine picks the minimal-quality-loss action that meets capacity target.
